title: Mémoire en chiffre du XIIe décembre 1560: anonymous report from the Agenais to Montmorency, BnF fr. 3157 no. 67

documents.shelfmark: BnF fr. 3157 no. 67, ff. 152r-156v (Gallica btv1b90598645 views 153-158)

plaintext.source: No decipherment on the leaves, the dorse or the neighbouring items; only the heading 'Du xiie decembre 1560' is in clear.

transcription.source: Gallica IIIF full resolution, half-width 3-line crops
transcription.notes: Tokens are cipher words (the manuscript divides words with '/'); 9,497 signs in all. First pass by three agents, then a key-guided correction pass by four agents against the images (corrections_<fol>.tsv, about 300 x->r fixes). 16 Nov 2026: all ten pages re-checked against full-resolution images by ten independent model checkers; merged signs separated (codes B, G, j, X, O), 379 words changed; 1,710 cipher words.

system.summary: Homophonic substitution in a cursive pseudo-script with word division, two-stroke units (zo=u, pp=m, s3=r, lz=d) and four whole-word codes (pour, roy, et, sieur). 16 Nov 2026: the signs first transcribed d and D are five signs (b, g, i; i, a), not polyphonic ones.
system.notes: Main trap: the rounder r-form (n) versus x (e). Delta and double dagger were first taken as polyphonic (u/v, b, g; i, a); the image check of 16 Nov 2026 showed three delta signs (b, g, i) and two crosses (i, a). No name codes; all persons and places spelt out.

prior_solution.where: G. Lasry solved it independently in 2023 (improved Feb 2026), unpublished (private communication, 25 Sept 2026). No DECODE record, not on Tomokiyo or Lasry (GL.htm) lists, no edition found by web search. Brunet 2019 on Clairac not reachable.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: posed the catalogue entry with /goal. No target-specific intervention.
tools: decrypt.py (key.txt with units and word codes)

solution.what: Located item 67 in fr. 3157: the BnF notice's folio numbers precede the item numbers, so the cipher is ff. 152r-156v (not f. 158). Fetched the ten pages from Gallica IIIF.
Checked the dorse and the neighbouring Villars letters for a decipherment or key: none.
Looked at Lasry's GL.htm tables for Henri II / Charles IX as the brief asked: different symbol sets.
Three agents transcribed the ten pages into ASCII sign codes (one stopped after three pages by a tool block; a fresh agent did 153v-154r).
One-sign-per-letter homophonic annealing with word spaces: gibberish (-4.2/char).
z followed by o in 262 of 283 cases: 'zo' taken as one unit; most frequent words Tzox, Wx, Wxm, hx.
Seeded Tzox=que, Wx/Wxm=le/les, hx=de; annealer read 'les derniers advertissemens', 'les affaires de pardeça'.
Aligned decrypted words with the French they must be: entendu (r=n, io=u), avoir, ordinairement (s3=r), souloit (nn=s); reran the annealer with these units (-3.2/char).
Standalone groups read from context as codes: Z=pour, 4=roy, c+/i+/e+=et, F/g=sieur.
Key-guided correction pass by four agents against the images, changing a sign only where the image supports it: about 300 x->r fixes, the looped sign y (=i) identified, missing signs restored.
Line-by-line reading with marked emendations; lz=d found during it (despuis, disans, d'environ); 16 of 1,715 cipher words left unread.
Web search for an edition or decipherment (names, places, shelfmark): none; Brunet 2019 on Clairac not reachable.

Merged with a parallel project pass on the same item (main 13e0f27b2): its margin (153r.14, 'assemblez en la chambre du conseil') and dorse ('Advertissemens') readings decoded with key.txt and confirmed; added to the reading.
Lasry review (email 25 Sept 2026): Lasry wrote that he had independently solved it in 2023 (improved Feb 2026) but never published it; kept in the ciphertext-only list with that note.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 7932 tokens, 52 types, fr-1530-despatches order 4: reading -2.115 per letter; random keys -5.3 (z 4.5); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -3.008 (mean -3.021, z 100.7); annealer on the real text -2.129. Verdict: weak.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): the ten corrected page transcriptions, the two line-by-line reading files and key.txt; Lasry's own 2023 solution is private and not in the repository.

Verification 3 (v3_below_b): flagged at 0.21 on reading_154v-156v.txt; the score counted the fol.line prefixes and the header. Both reading files cut to their text score 0.755 explicit holes / 0.54 plain (1560 spelling), hole rate 0.073; sentences hold. Kept read; reading field set to the two files.
Read bar applied per document (v10): 1 of 1 documents marked read measure under 95% of words read as sense (v2_score explicit holes) and are now read in part; read_share recorded for each.

Audit of the reading against the mechanical decrypt, after C. Pierrot and C. Desenclos (The Conversation, 10 Nov 2026) published a figure of the reveal of f. 152v lines 9-14 with the letters circled where the key's letter is not the reading's. mark_emendations.py aligned each reading line with key.txt applied to the transcription, letter by letter (u/v, i/j, i/y, accents and word division not counted; second values of d, D, c counted apart). Result: 362 of 1,709 words depart from the decrypt, against 108 marked before; 331 letters emended, 163 supplied, 236 decrypt letters not taken up, 224 second values of polyphonic signs. All are now bracketed in the reading files, the mechanical decrypt is published as decrypt_mechanical.txt, and the reveal marks each departing sign. read_share falls from 0.94 to 0.80. Their figure is correct for this passage.

The passage of the article's figure checked on a full-resolution crop of f. 152v (openapi.bnf.fr). Two transcription slips corrected where the reading was already right: 152v.12 +rppxrQ to +yppxrQ (aiment), 152v.14 xzxfzoQxss to x3xfzoQxss (executer). The sign d (delta) is one shape for b and g; the double-barred cross is one shape for a and i; the third stroke of the group fed is a hook, not the delta. envoyoit, disans and faisoit not settled at this resolution. The other nine pages not rechecked.

All ten pages re-checked against full-resolution images (openapi.bnf.fr), one independent model checker per page, each told to change a sign only where the image shows another (image_check/). They classed 192 words as transcription slips, 175 as image-matches-transcription, 47 unclear, 49 as reading wrong, 27 as signs missing or extra. All ten found that the code d covered three signs (barred delta = b, tall curled delta = g, crossed delta = i) and D two (tall double dagger = i, short cross = a), and that an o-sign had been written x, y or 3x. New codes B, G, j, X, O added; 379 words of the transcription changed. The main claim was confirmed by eye on f. 156v lines 1-3 and f. 155v line 26. The checkers were shown the reading; not a blind transcription.

Reading re-aligned with the key applied to the corrected transcription, no sign allowed a second value: 1,474 of 1,703 words read exactly as the key gives (1,347 of 1,709 before, with three signs allowed two values); 229 bracketed. 34 lines of the reading corrected where the checked signs give another word (e.g. 'n'ont seignurie, place ni chasteau', 'je ne faicts doubte', 'aiant', 'fierez', 'aurez'); 4 unread words resolved (15 to 11). read_share 0.80 to 0.865.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py) rerun on 16 Nov 2026 on the corrected transcription (7,932 read tokens, 52 types): the reading scores -2.115 a letter (-2.264 before), random keys -5.300 (z 4.5), keys fitted to shuffled ciphertext -3.021 at best -3.008, and the annealer started from a random key on the real text reaches -2.129 (-2.657 before), close to the reading. Polyphony 0.024 (0.046 before). The tool's verdict stays "weak": the reading is 4.5 sd above random keys and the pass mark is 5.

outcome.method_basis: The homophonic cipher with two-stroke units of BnF fr. 3157 item 67 (ff. 152r-156v) was broken from the images alone: 'zo' taken as one unit from statistics, probable short words (que, le, les, de) seeded into an annealer, then words aligned against the French they had to be; no decipherment, key or edition exists.

outcome.fraction_read_source: reading_152r-154r.txt + reading_154v-156v.txt against the corrected transcription: 11 words marked [..] out of 1,710 cipher words (99.4%). This counts words given a reading. Words exactly as the key gives them: 1,474 of 1,703 (86.6%); 229 depart from the mechanical decrypt and are bracketed (79 whole, 150 with letters). emendations.json has the counts and the per-sign table.
outcome.notes: Key broken here ciphertext-only. Content fits the Agenais in Dec 1560: Clairac assembly, Caumont, Biron at Bergerac, Navarre at Nérac, the États of Orléans deputies. Writer unnamed. 16 Nov 2026: an audit against the mechanical decrypt found 362 words departing from it (108 had been marked). An image check of all ten pages then showed that the first transcription had merged signs: d was three signs (B = b, G = g, j = i), D two (D = i, X = a), and an o-sign had been written x or y. With the corrected transcription 28 signs, 92% of the text, each give one letter in 90% or more of their uses and 229 words still depart from the key. 34 lines of the reading were corrected. The checkers saw the reading, so this is not a blind transcription. Statistical validation rerun on the corrected transcription: reading -2.115 a letter, annealer from a random key on the real text -2.129 (was -2.657), shuffled refit -3.021; verdict label still weak. No check outside the project (Lasry's unpublished solution not compared).

texts.label: Mémoire en chiffre, 12 Dec 1560, ff. 152r-156v
texts.summary: An anonymous report to the connétable de Montmorency from a Catholic gentleman of the Agenais, a neighbour of the sieur de Fumel, dated 12 December 1560, a week after the death of François II. It reports Protestant preaching and the rebel assembly at Clairac, the conduct of the king of Navarre ('le chief') at Nérac, Biron and the rebel captains, and the writer's fear for his life.

reading_review.note: v3 check 23 Oct 2026: the sweep scored only reading_154v-156v.txt with its fol.line prefixes; both reading files, prefixes and header cut, score 0.755 on explicit holes (111/147 sentences; each half 0.76), 0.54 plain (1560 spelling the word list lacks), hole rate 0.073. What it rests on: the key broken here from the ciphertext (homophonic, two-stroke units, four code words), the decrypt read line by line on the ten page images with 108 words emended in brackets and 16 left unread; no contemporary decipherment, no copy, no print (Lasry's unpublished 2023 solution not seen). READING.md is a normalised editorial version and is not the reading scored. 16 Nov 2026: the count of 108 emendations was an undercount. A letter-by-letter alignment of the reading with the mechanical decrypt finds 362 words that depart from it (emendations.tsv); all are now bracketed. The reading as sentences is unchanged; the explicit-hole sentence score with all brackets counted is 0.326 (45/138). 16 Nov 2026, later: all ten pages re-checked against the images; d and D were several signs each and are now coded apart; 34 lines of the reading corrected to what the signs give; 229 words bracketed, hole rate 0.135, sentences 0.568 (83/146).

texts.note: 16 Nov 2026: every departure of the reading from the mechanical decrypt (key.txt applied to the transcription, decrypt_mechanical.txt) is in brackets (mark_emendations.py), and no sign is allowed a second value. After the image check of all ten pages, 1,474 of the 1,703 words read are exactly what the key gives; 229 carry a bracket (79 whole words, 150 with one or more letters), 11 are unread. With every bracketed word or part-word counted as a hole, 86.5% of the words read as sense (v2_score, hole rate 0.135; 0.568 of sentences clean). Coherent sentences, under the 95% read bar: read in part.
